generalfeedback: If \[\int f(x) dx = F(x)\] then \[\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b).\] So, in order to calculate the definite integral of {{CT:5}} with respect to {{CT:6}} we first calculate its integral (Note: we don't need to consider a constant of integration): \[\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} = {{CT:7}}.\] So, let \[F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:7}}\] Then, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:8}} - {{CT:9}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:10}} \end{array}\] and \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int^{{CT:4}}_{{CT:0}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle F({{CT:4}}) - F({{CT:0}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:11}}-{{CT:8}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:12}} \end{array}\] So, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} + \int^{{CT:4}}_{{CT:0}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:10}}+ {{CT:12}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:13}} \end{array}\]
